dedupe_keys.name: u s census bureau national population projections 2023 series

description: The National Population Projections of the U.S. Census Bureau estimate the future resident population of the United States with the cohort-component method, starting from a base consistent with the latest decennial census and population estimates. The 2023 series provides projected population by age, sex, race, Hispanic origin and nativity, with projected births, deaths and net international migration, for a main series and alternative migration scenarios (high, low and zero immigration), from 2022 to 2100. Coverage: national only; states and counties are not projected by this program. Earlier series (2012, 2014, 2017) remain available, and several are in the Census Data API (popproj group). Format and access: CSV datasets and XLSX tables to download; free and public domain. Caveats: projections are conditional on the fertility, mortality and migration assumptions, and the page notes that the Vintage 2025 estimates showed growth slowing to 0.5 per cent because of lower net international migration, which the 2023 main series predates. Simulation uses: long-horizon demand scenarios for infrastructure capacity planning, climate adaptation studies and national energy, water and transport outlooks that need population to 2100 with alternative migration paths. Related records: Population and Housing Unit Estimates (the base), the International Database (projections for other countries to 2100) and EIA's Annual Energy Outlook, which uses population as a driver.
